interfaces.description:
Interfaces lists the network interfaces to capture on, e.g.
["eth0", "eth1"]. The special value "auto" resolves to the interface
of the default route at startup.

Naming an interface fed by a switch's mirror/SPAN port makes Skopos
see the whole LAN's traffic rather than only this machine's — see
capture.mirror.

private_ranges.description:
PrivateRanges are the CIDR ranges treated as "internal" when
classifying traffic (LAN↔WAN, LAN↔LAN) and choosing block behaviour.
Defaults to RFC 1918, IPv6 ULA and link-local ranges.

network.description:
Network groups address-classification settings shared by capture,
detection and the firewall.

hot.description:
Hot is the fast storage path (SSD): SQLite database and runtime
state. Mount this on your SSD volume.

cold.description:
Cold is the archive path (HDD or NAS share) for the daily database
backup. Skopos keeps running when this path is unavailable; the
backup is skipped and reported.

hot_max_size.description:
HotMaxSize caps hot-storage usage. When the cap is reached the oldest
raw flows are deleted first; aggregated rollups are kept.

spool_max_size.description:
SpoolMaxSize is reserved for a spool buffer that does not exist yet.
It is accepted so existing configuration files keep loading, and has
no effect. Nothing is spooled today.

raw_flows.description:
RawFlows is how long individual flow records stay in the database
before they are deleted. The rollups outlive them.

rollup_1m.description: Rollup1m is how long 1-minute aggregates are kept.

rollup_1h.description: Rollup1h is how long 1-hour aggregates are kept.

rollup_1d.description:
Rollup1d is how long daily aggregates are kept. "0" keeps them
forever.

alerts.description:
Alerts is how long alerts and the incidents grouping them are kept.
Every other table had a bound and this one did not, so on a NAS whose
disk is also the household's storage the alert history was the one
thing that grew for as long as Skopos ran. An incident is deleted
with the last of its alerts, never before, so the Alerts view never
offers an episode whose events are gone. "0" keeps them forever.

retention.description:
Retention controls how long each data resolution is kept on hot
storage before it is deleted.

archive_at.description:
ArchiveAt is reserved for an export-to-cold job that does not exist
yet. It is accepted so existing configuration files keep loading, and
has no effect. Raw flows past their retention are deleted, not
exported; the daily backup is the durable copy.

enabled.description: Enabled turns the daily database backup to cold storage on or off.

keep.description: Keep is the number of backup generations retained on cold storage.

at.description: At is the local time of day the backup runs.

backup.description: Backup configures the daily SQLite online backup to cold storage.

storage.description:
Storage configures the hot (SSD) and cold (HDD/NAS) data paths and
how long data is retained at each resolution.

sample_threshold_pps.description:
SampleThresholdPPS is the packets-per-second rate above which
adaptive sampling kicks in to protect the NAS CPU. The transition is
reported as a system event, never silent. "0" disables sampling.

dns.description:
DNS enables parsing DNS responses (names only) so the dashboard can
show hostnames instead of bare IPs. Turning it off stops the parser
reading them at all — nothing is filtered after the fact — so the
household's lookups are not recorded anywhere. mDNS answers go with
it: a printer announcing itself is then filed by address and MAC
rather than as "printer.local".

sni.description:
SNI enables parsing TLS ClientHello server names (metadata only).
Turning it off stops the ClientHello being read at all, which also
ends the JA4 client fingerprint — it comes out of the same handshake
— so device pages show no fingerprints.

rdns.description:
RDNS is reserved for reverse-DNS lookups that do not exist yet. It is
accepted so existing configuration files keep loading, and has no
effect. No address is ever looked up in reverse today; the names in
the dashboard come from observed DNS answers and TLS SNI, which
capture.dns and capture.sni govern.

devices.description:
Devices enables the LAN device inventory built from ARP/NDP traffic
and mDNS/DHCP names. Required by the new_device detector.

flow_flush.description:
FlowFlush is how often aggregated flow counters are flushed from
memory to the database.

flow_idle_timeout.description:
FlowIdleTimeout is reserved for an idle-expiry rule that does not
exist yet. It is accepted so existing configuration files keep
loading, and has no effect. Every open flow is flushed on the
flow_flush tick whether it has been silent or not.

interfaces.description:
Interfaces are fed by a switch's mirror/SPAN port, or a tap: they
carry other devices' traffic, not this machine's. Declaring them
changes nothing about how packets are captured — it tells Skopos that
what it sees is the whole segment, so the dashboard can say plainly
that visibility is network-wide while blocking still only acts on
traffic passing this machine's kernel.

mirror.description:
Mirror declares which interfaces carry mirrored traffic from a
switch's SPAN port or a tap.

capture.description: Capture tunes packet capture and metadata enrichment.

enabled.description: Enabled turns the detector on or off.

window.description:
Window is the sliding time window for counting distinct ports and
targets.

ports.description:
Ports is the number of distinct destination ports on a single target
that triggers a vertical-scan alert.

targets.description:
Targets is the number of distinct targets on the same port that
triggers a horizontal-scan alert.

external.description: External holds thresholds for sources outside the private ranges.

ports.description:
Ports is the number of distinct destination ports on a single target
that triggers a vertical-scan alert.

targets.description:
Targets is the number of distinct targets on the same port that
triggers a horizontal-scan alert.

internal.description:
Internal holds thresholds for sources inside the private ranges
(set higher: legitimate LAN tools scan more).

severity.description: Severity assigned to port-scan alerts: info, warning or critical.

block.description:
Block requests an automatic block for offending sources. Only acts
when firewall.enforcement is "enforce".

portscan.description:
Portscan detects vertical scans (many ports on one target) and
horizontal scans (one port across many targets).

enabled.description: Enabled turns the detector on or off.

max_new_connections.description:
MaxNewConnections is the number of new connections from one source
within the window that triggers an alert.

max_packets_per_second.description:
MaxPacketsPerSecond is the sustained packet rate from one source
that triggers an alert.

severity.description: Severity assigned to rate alerts: info, warning or critical.

block.description:
Block requests an automatic block for offending sources. Only acts
when firewall.enforcement is "enforce".

rate.description: Rate detects connection floods and abnormal packet rates per source.

enabled.description:
Enabled turns feed matching on or off. Recommended when the NAS is
reachable from the internet; in a pure LAN it mostly produces noise.

lists.description:
Lists selects the feeds: the built-in names "firehol_level1" and
"spamhaus_drop", or any https:// URL serving one CIDR per line.

refresh.description: Refresh is how often feeds are re-downloaded.

severity.description: Severity assigned to feed-hit alerts: info, warning or critical.

block.description:
Block requests an automatic block for feed-listed peers. Only acts
when firewall.enforcement is "enforce".

feeds.description:
Feeds matches traffic against public IP blocklists (FireHOL Level 1,
Spamhaus DROP) refreshed at runtime.

enabled.description: Enabled turns the detector on or off (requires capture.devices).

severity.description: Severity assigned to new-device alerts: info, warning or critical.

new_device.description: NewDevice raises an alert when an unknown device appears in the LAN.

cooldown.description:
Cooldown is the minimum interval between notifications for the same
(detector, source) pair; additional hits are counted and included in
the next notification instead of spamming.

enabled.description: Enabled turns quiet hours on or off.

from.description: From is the local start time of the quiet window.

to.description: To is the local end time of the quiet window (may cross midnight).

min_severity.description:
MinSeverity is the lowest severity still delivered during quiet
hours: info, warning or critical.

quiet_hours.description:
QuietHours suppresses notifications below a minimum severity during
a nightly time window.

detection.description:
Detection configures the detectors that decide what counts as
suspicious, and how alerts are throttled.

enforcement.description:
Enforcement is the global switch: "observe" logs every block
decision without touching the kernel (the shipping default), while
"enforce" applies blocks through the backend. Arm it deliberately
after watching the observe log for a while.

backend.description:
Backend selects the firewall implementation. "nftables" (the only
backend in v1) manages a dedicated "inet skopos" table via netlink.

block_ttl.description:
BlockTTL is the default lifetime of automatic blocks; they expire in
the kernel via nftables set timeouts. Manual blocks default to
permanent. "0" makes automatic blocks permanent too.

action_external.description:
ActionExternal is what happens to blocked traffic from outside the
private ranges: "drop" (silent) or "reject" (immediate error).

action_internal.description:
ActionInternal is what happens to blocked traffic from inside the
private ranges: "drop" or "reject" ("reject" fails fast and is
friendlier when a LAN block turns out to be a mistake).

allowlist.description:
Allowlist lists IPs/CIDRs that are never blocked, not even by feeds.
The default gateway is always protected in addition to this list.

blocklist.description:
Blocklist lists IPs/CIDRs that are always blocked while enforcement
is "enforce" — declarative, versionable static blocks.

firewall.description: Firewall configures blocking behaviour and the nftables backend.

url.description:
URL is the base URL of the ntfy server, e.g.
"https://ntfy.example.com" or "https://ntfy.sh". Empty disables ntfy.

topic.description: Topic is the ntfy topic to publish to.

token.description:
Token is an ntfy access token (sent as Bearer). Supports ${ENV}
interpolation so secrets can stay out of the file.

username.description: Username enables HTTP basic auth as an alternative to Token.

password.description: Password is the basic-auth password. Supports ${ENV} interpolation.

ntfy.description:
Ntfy configures push notifications through a self-hosted ntfy server
or ntfy.sh (same API).

url.description: URL receives a JSON POST per alert. Empty disables the webhook.

webhook.description: Webhook posts every alert as JSON to a URL of your choice.

enabled.description: Enabled turns system notifications on or off.

system.description:
System controls operational notifications (start after crash,
firewall degraded, cold storage unreachable, feed update failed,
update available).

notify.description: Notify configures alert delivery (ntfy and a generic webhook).

bind.description:
Bind is the listen address. With network_mode: host this is a real
host address; keep 0.0.0.0 unless you know you need otherwise.

port.description:
Port is the web/API port. With network_mode: host there is no port
mapping — this is the port your browser connects to.

external_url.description:
ExternalURL is the address under which you reach the dashboard from
your devices (used as the click target of push notifications), e.g.
"https://skopos.example.com" or "http://192.168.1.10:8686".

mode.description:
Mode is "single_admin" (username + Argon2 hash below), or "none"
(only for trusted LANs — Skopos logs a prominent warning). Default:
"single_admin" as soon as password_hash is set, otherwise "none".

username.description: Username is the admin login name.

password_hash.description:
PasswordHash is the Argon2id hash of the admin password. Generate it
with: skopos hash-password

session_ttl.description: SessionTTL is how long a login session stays valid.

auth.description: Auth configures dashboard and API authentication.

name.description: Name identifies the token in the audit log.

token.description:
Token is the secret value (sent as "Authorization: Bearer …").
Supports ${ENV} interpolation.

items.description: APIToken is a named API token.

tokens.description:
Tokens are named API tokens for automation (scripts, Home
Assistant). Scope "read" allows GET, "write" also allows mutations.

cert.description: Cert is the path to the PEM certificate chain.

key.description: Key is the path to the PEM private key.

tls.description:
TLS serves HTTPS directly from Skopos. Usually you terminate TLS at
a reverse proxy instead and leave this empty.

trusted_proxies.description:
TrustedProxies lists the networks — in CIDR form, e.g. "127.0.0.1/32"
or "172.18.0.0/16" — whose X-Forwarded-For header Skopos will believe.
Leave it empty, the default, unless Skopos really does sit behind a
reverse proxy.

The header costs nothing to forge. Honouring it from any source lets a
single attacker present a fresh address on every request, and the login
rate limiter — which counts failures per address — then never counts to
two. Connections from outside these networks are identified by the
address they actually came from.

server.description: Server configures the web dashboard, API, authentication and TLS.

level.description: Level is one of debug, info, warn, error.

file.description:
File enables structured JSON logs in <storage.cold>/logs/skopos.log,
in addition to the readable stdout log. Container stdout dies with the
container, which is exactly when an incident is worth reading about,
so this is the copy that survives a restart. Cold storage is allowed
to be missing: Skopos then logs one warning and keeps monitoring
rather than refusing to start.

max_size.description:
MaxSize is the size at which the current log file is rotated to
skopos.log.1. "0" disables rotation, letting the file grow.

max_backups.description:
MaxBackups is the number of rotated log files to keep. "0" keeps
none: rotation then simply starts an empty file.

logging.description: Logging configures log verbosity and file logging to cold storage.

metrics.description: Metrics configures the optional Prometheus endpoint.

check.description:
Check asks GitHub's public releases endpoint once a day whether a
newer Skopos exists, shows the answer in the System view and sends one
notification per new version. Nothing is transmitted but the request
itself. On by default — a monitoring tool that silently runs a stale
image is worse than one that asks.

updates.description: Updates configures the daily release check.

demo.description:
Demo replaces live capture with a synthetic traffic generator so the
dashboard can be explored without any privileges or real traffic.

title: Skopos configuration
description: Config is the root of config.yaml.
